items_missed: Set Agenda: never asked 'how are you today,' gave no agenda statement (what he'd cover / how long it'd take), no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.

Probe: never got zip codes at either the origin house or the destination storage unit, didn't ask about special considerations like narrow hallways/tight turns, never asked about packing service needs, never asked if there's anything the customer is worried about with the move.
Pricing/Differentiators: no 'pricing is super simple' opener before launching into the rate.
Estimate: no walk-distance variable mentioned, no equivalents used (school-bus comparison, etc.), no traffic variable addressed.
Save Your Ass: entire section missing — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no close.

Quote/Booking: never said 'no deposit required,' didn't ask the customer to reply with corrections on the emailed quote, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?', and the bolded-list-in-email can't be confirmed from the transcript.
Politeness: only used the customer's first name (Alex) twice — short of the 3+ threshold.

Bonus: missed a Sparefoot/storage referral opportunity right when the customer said he hadn't purchased the storage unit yet; no rapport-building humor; insurance explanation covered the $2,000 No Worries coverage but skipped the 60 cents/lb baseline.
top_strength: Rance ran a clean, fast inventory intake and then gave one of the more complete pricing walkthroughs in this batch unprompted — hourly rate, trip fees, damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee all landed in a single clear pass, and he even proactively framed a budget number: "about $655 would probably be a reasonable budget for your move."
coaching_note: Rance, your pricing walkthrough here is genuinely strong — transparent, complete, and you hit both Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee without being prompted. But you skipped the two things that build trust and protect this customer's bill: no agenda upfront ('here's what we'll cover, sound good?') and zero Save Your Ass — that's the section that actually shortens moves and lowers costs, and it cost you all 10 points. Get in the habit of grabbing zip codes on both ends, and close every call with 'no deposit required' and 'any other questions before I let you go' — those are easy points you're leaving on the table.
phone_presence_notes: Friendly, casual filler ('easy peasy,' 'right on, cool') carried the tone, but transitions were mechanical — he moved from answer to next question without acknowledging what the customer actually said.
